summary: Every journalled event carries a privacy class derived from the stream id the bridge already labelled, and private communications are excluded from every prompt and every tool result unless their own source is opted in

coordination.notes: Derived from the stream id, never from a second pass over the text. A regex hunting for the word whispers would be a second classifier free to disagree with the first, and the one it would disagree about is the one that must not leak. An unknown channel defaults to private-player rather than public-game: a channel nobody has decided about is not publishable because nobody got round to it, and defaulting an undecided thing to the most shareable class is how a new private channel reaches a prompt the day the game adds one. Capture stays continuous - the whisper is journalled - which is what makes an opt-in retroactively meaningful. The filter drops the whole event rather than only its text: a sequence number is a pointer at a whisper, and a model given the pointer plus observations.read would have the words.
coordination.deviations: Two checks written for G4 asserted the pre-G12 behaviour ('three events came back', and one reading private-comms out of a tool result). They were changed rather than worked around, and it is named here because editing a test to make your own change pass is indistinguishable from a bug unless somebody says so. The opt-in is read from drc.ai-share-sources.v1 rather than being a parameter nothing sets: without a stored value the opt-in branch could not be executed in the running app at all, only in a test, and a branch nobody can trigger is a branch nobody can prove. A Settings control on top of that key is not built. The key is named drc.ai-share-sources.v1 rather than the more obvious drc.ai-privacy-optin.v1 because gitleaks scores the latter above its generic-api-key entropy threshold (3.708) and blocks the commit - trap 3's documented false positive, renamed rather than bypassed with --no-verify.
